title: Live stream: bearer token in ClientHello, checked by the Account extractor's code
description:
Epic mimid-e64f; docs/design/binary-live-stream.md §5.3, §9 question 2.

Readings: (a) the bearer token on the WebSocket upgrade's Authorization header, which reuses the JMAP Account extractor unchanged but cannot be set by browsers' WebSocket API; (b) the token in the ClientHello.

Chosen (Mark, 2026-11-20): (b), checked by the same code as the JMAP Account extractor (crates/mimid-server/src/jmap/auth.rs), so the JMAP boundary keeps one check.

Added by the agent for mimid-e64f (INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC):
- A bad, unknown or revoked token is answered with Error code "unauthorized" without id, and the connection closes; every refusal looks the same, as on JMAP.
- The token is checked again before each request and each batch of Delivers, so a token revoked while connected is refused the same way.
- A client that sends no ClientHello within 10 seconds of the upgrade is closed.
